 What Bobby Moynihan Watches (and Listens to) With His Daughters
 By Bobby Moynihan As told to Marah Eakin 
 Nov. 17, 2026 
 Save this article to read it later.
 Find this story in your account’s ‘Saved for Later’ section.
 Photo-Illustration: Vulture; Photos: Getty Images, Everett Collection, Netflix, Focus Features, Walt Disney, Amazon Prime Video 
 Bobby Moynihan loves being a dad so much that, when he signs on to Zoom for this interview, he’s wearing a shirt covered in his youngest daughter Dorothy’s face. It’s one of those mock rap-style shirts , with five pictures of the preschooler set above her big purple name. It’s adorable.
 Moynihan’s wife gave him two of the shirts for Father’s Day — one for each daughter — and Moynihan says he wears them so often he tends to forget whose face he’s hyping until someone points it out. When he wears Dorothy’s shirt, Moynihan says, his 3-year-old is stoked, but when he once tried to wear 9-year-old Diana’s to pick her up at school, he says he got a classic tween “Can you not?”
 Fortunately for Diana, Dorothy, and their mom, there are already rap-style T-shirts bearing their dad’s face for sale on Etsy , so should they ever want to rep him while they’re out and about, it will be easy enough. And why wouldn’t they, really? With the second season of The Fall and Rise of Reggie Dinkins just starting to air on NBC and Moynihan’s surprise recent drop-in on SNL as both Drunk Uncle and David S. Pumpkins’s skeletal pal, Dorothy and Diana’s dad certainly seems to be having a moment.
 .
 Coraline and Stranger Things 
 Photo: Focus Features/Everett Collection 
 My 9-year-old is very into Coraline , Tim Burton, all that kind of spooky stuff.
 She wants to watch Stranger Things , but we won’t allow it. But she still watches behind-the-scenes videos of Stranger Things , I think because she knows she can’t watch it, but she still wants to know how they’re making it. She could also be processing that this is my job, like since I’m in this business she gets that those are actors in Stranger Things , not real kids.
 She wants to watch M3gan , too, but we’re like, “There’s no way.” She even wanted to watch something called Murder Drones the other day, and I was like, “Well, okay, we’ve got to have a conversation about that, I guess.”
 We asked her what she wanted to see one night and she said, “Can I watch Insidious: The Red Door ?,” which was just like “What?” We ended up saying, “No, but thank you for making our night.”
 I don’t even know who some of these things they make now are for, really. Like, who really wants to watch Freddy Fazbear ? Who needs a horror thing about a kids’ animatronic restaurant that has come to life, but with no real gore? It’s so weird, but she loves it.
 I mean, I guess when I was a kid I was watching Stand by Me , where a bunch of kids find a dead body, so who knows?
 .
 KPop Demon Hunters and Katseye
 Photo: Kristy Sparow/Getty Images 
 My 3-year-old is very into KPop Demon Hunters and has been for a while. She’s a full pop star.
 We listen to lots of Katseye with her, too. In college, I was dating a girl who was super into the Spice Girls, and then we went to a Spice Girls concert because she won tickets on the radio. After that, I became fascinated by the Spice Girls for a couple of months, just like the idea that somebody put together this team of people and now they have a movie and songs. So since I wildly enjoy a put-together band of people, Katseye is very entertaining to me.
 Having a 9-year-old and then a 3-year-old, though, both of whom fell in love with the group in different periods of their career, is interesting. They seem to be transitioning into a Pussycat Dolls kind of situation rather than a Sabrina Carpenter situation, which is very fascinating. But that being said, she knows every single one of those dance moves. We do that together, and that’s fun. It’s exercise and it’s wonderful and she’s a great dancer.
 When Katseye was recently on SNL , that was when I got to see the first glint in her eye of, like, “Wait a minute. They’re on SNL ? That’s your old job.” She doesn’t really know what the show is yet, but she knows I used to work there, so it was like, “Can you have them come here, too?” I had to say, “I haven’t been on the show in ten years. That’s not how it works.”
 .
 Mulan 
 Photo: Walt Disney/Everett Collection 
 Recently they freaked when I met Ming-Na Wen, who was absolutely wonderful. She made a video as the voice of Mulan because my daughters love Mulan — especially the 3-year-old, who’s been dressed as Mulan for 90 percent of her life and was actually wearing a Mulan dress when I was like “Hey, I have something to show you” and played the video. Because she’s 3 she didn’t completely get it, but the 9-year-old was kind of blown away, so now I have that.
 My daughters love a warrior, which makes sense since my 3-year-old is a badass and the 9-year-old is a sneaky demon in a good way.
 .
 The Lonely Island
 Photo: Charles Sykes/Bravo/NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal via Getty Images 
 I haven’t really tried to show them things that I think are funny yet, but I can’t wait. Even stuff from SNL , I can’t wait for them to organically find the show and go, “What is that?” Like, “We know you were on it because your office is filled with bobbleheads.”
 I guess I’ve shown them a couple of cartoons I liked as a kid and stuff like that, but I really try not to force anything on them. I am a fan of things, and I don’t want it to be like, “You have to like this, and that’s it.” My dad was like, “You’re a Giants fan and that’s it.” I want them to be able to like what they want, and they have. I mean, my wife and I always talk about how it’s so crazy that our older daughter gravitated towards spooky Halloween stuff, because neither of us are like that.
 I will say, the other day my daughter took a thing and threw it on the ground and said, “ I threw it on the ground ,” like she was quoting a Lonely Island sketch that I’m in, and that was bonkers. Just the best. Very few of those sketches are appropriate for kids, but they’re all pretty great. They’re just pure love and joy. Those guys want to make people laugh.
 .
 Frozen 
 Photo: Walt Disney Co./Everett Collection 
 Right now, we’re in a late, odd Frozen period. Our 3-year-old all of a sudden has found Frozen , so that’s back in our life. So Frozen Look and Find is a very big thing right before bed, and she wants to hear Anna and Elsa in some adventure on her Toniebox.
 Tonieboxes are great except for when your kid sleeps with you, it is absolutely insane to try and fall asleep listening to one play 45 minutes of not the voice actors from the movie.
 It’s weird to be back in Frozen- land because it automatically brings me back to COVID and Frozen 2 , because that was huge for my 9-year-old at whatever age she was during the pandemic.
